paragraphs.title: The Yoke as a Symbol of Babylonian Rule

easy.explanation: The LORD told Jeremiah to make bonds and yokes and put them on his neck.
easy.q: What did the LORD command Jeremiah to make?

answers: To the kings of the surrounding nations
To the people of Babylon only
easy.explanation: They were to be sent to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon.
easy.q: To whom were the bonds and yokes to be sent?

easy.explanation: They were sent by the messengers who came to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah.
easy.q: By whose hand were the bonds and yokes sent?

answers: Babylonian rule and submission to it
medium.explanation: The yoke represented submission to the authority of the king of Babylon.
medium.q: What did the yokes symbolize in this passage?

medium.explanation: The messengers came to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah.
medium.q: Which king of Judah is mentioned in these verses?

answers: A wooden device placed upon the neck
medium.explanation: A yoke was a device placed upon the neck, symbolizing control and service.
medium.q: What is a yoke in the context of these verses?

answers: It concerned several nations, not Judah alone
The messengers were the kings themselves
challenge.explanation: The message was directed to the rulers of several surrounding kingdoms.
challenge.q: What does the list of several kings suggest about Jeremiah’s message?

answers: It was given after Babylon had fallen
It is dated to Jehoiakim’s reign but appears to be enacted in Zedekiah’s time
The messengers arrived before Jeremiah was born
challenge.explanation: Verse 1 dates the word to the beginning of Jehoiakim’s reign, while verse 3 places the messengers before Zedekiah.
challenge.q: What apparent chronological difficulty is associated with this prophecy?

answers: A yoke represents submission to a ruler
A yoke was used only for decoration
challenge.explanation: A yoke placed on the neck clearly pictures subjection to another authority.
challenge.q: Why was a yoke an appropriate symbol for Babylonian authority?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I have made the earth, the man and the beast.”
easy.q: Who is described as having made the earth, man, and beast?

easy.explanation: The LORD gave all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
easy.q: Into whose hand did the LORD give all these lands?

answers: It would be made a kingdom
It would suffer the sword, famine, and pestilence
easy.explanation: The LORD says such a nation would be punished with the sword, famine, and pestilence.
easy.q: What punishment would come upon a nation that would not serve Babylon?

answers: He is sovereign over creation and the nations
He has no authority over kings
medium.explanation: As Creator, the LORD has authority to give lands to whomever He sees fit.
medium.q: What does the LORD’s claim to have made the earth show about Him?

medium.explanation: The nations would serve Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his son’s son.
medium.q: How many generations are named in the period of Babylon’s rule?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the LORD’s own judgment and decision.
medium.q: What does “unto whom it seemed meet unto me” mean?

answers: Its rule would continue only until the appointed time of its land
challenge.explanation: Babylon’s authority would continue only until the appointed time came.
challenge.q: What limitation on Babylon’s rule is stated in these verses?

answers: Refusal leads to punishment by sword, famine, and pestilence
challenge.explanation: The passage directly connects refusal to serve Babylon with these punishments.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between refusing Babylon’s yoke and punishment?

answers: The extensive scope of Nebuchadnezzar’s given authority
challenge.explanation: The mention of the beasts emphasizes how broad the authority granted to him was.
challenge.q: What does the mention of “the beasts of the field” emphasize?

answers: Prophets, diviners, dreamers, enchanters, and sorcerers
easy.explanation: The passage lists prophets, diviners, dreamers, enchanters, and sorcerers.
easy.q: Whom were the people told not to heed?

answers: They should serve the king of Babylon
They should not serve the king of Babylon
easy.explanation: They said, “Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon.”
easy.q: What did these false speakers say?

answers: They would be removed from the land and perish
They would receive the temple vessels
easy.explanation: The lie would cause them to be driven from the land and perish.
easy.q: What would happen to those who followed the false message?

answers: They falsely promised that Babylon need not be served
They did not know where Jerusalem was
They wanted to rebuild the temple
medium.explanation: Their promise that the people would not serve Babylon was a lie.
medium.q: Why did Jeremiah warn the people not to listen to these speakers?

medium.explanation: Jeremiah says, “I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah.”
medium.q: To which king did Jeremiah also speak according to these words?

answers: One who seeks hidden or future knowledge
medium.explanation: A diviner is someone who practices divination or attempts to discover the future.
medium.q: What is a diviner in this passage?

answers: Removal from the land and destruction
challenge.explanation: The false message would lead to being driven out of the land and perishing.
challenge.q: What twofold result is associated with believing the false prophecy?

answers: They claimed to speak for God without being commissioned by Him
challenge.explanation: Although they prophesied in the LORD’s name, He had not sent them.
challenge.q: What does the LORD emphasize by saying, “I have not sent them”?

answers: All could be deceived by the same false promise
All of them had already gone to Babylon
challenge.explanation: The king and the surrounding nations alike needed warning against the false message.
challenge.q: Why was the warning directed both to Zedekiah and to the nations?

answers: The priests and all the people
easy.explanation: Jeremiah spoke to the priests and to all the people.
easy.q: To whom did Jeremiah speak concerning the vessels of the LORD’s house?

answers: They would soon be brought back
easy.explanation: They said that the vessels of the LORD’s house would shortly be brought again from Babylon.
easy.q: What did the prophets claim about the vessels taken to Babylon?

answers: Prevent the remaining vessels from being taken
easy.explanation: If they were prophets, they should intercede so that the vessels left in Jerusalem would not go to Babylon.
easy.q: What did Jeremiah say the prophets should ask the LORD to do?

answers: He warned that the remaining vessels would be taken away
medium.explanation: Jeremiah declared that the vessels still remaining would go to Babylon.
medium.q: Why did Jeremiah call the promise of a quick return a lie?

answers: They should intercede to prevent the remaining vessels from being taken
medium.explanation: He challenged them to make intercession to the LORD concerning the vessels.
medium.q: What test did Jeremiah present to the prophets?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the vessels still present in the LORD’s house, the king’s house, and Jerusalem.
medium.q: What does “the vessels which are left” mean?

answers: They promised a quick return, while he warned of further removal
They warned of exile, while he promised a quick return
They spoke about Egypt, while he spoke about Tyrus
challenge.explanation: The false prophets promised restoration soon, but Jeremiah warned that the remaining vessels would be taken.
challenge.q: What was the difference between the false prophets’ promise and Jeremiah’s message?

answers: The warning concerned both religious leaders and the whole community
Only the priests were responsible for the vessels
The people knew nothing about the prophets
challenge.explanation: By addressing both groups, Jeremiah included leaders and the entire public.
challenge.q: What does Jeremiah’s address to the priests and all the people imply?

answers: A true message from the LORD should be tested by what actually happens
Every prophet must also be a king
Prophets are not allowed to pray
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah challenged them to demonstrate their claim by interceding concerning the predicted event.
challenge.q: What is the significance of Jeremiah’s challenge to the prophets?

paragraphs.title: The Exile and Future Return of the Vessels

answers: The pillars, the sea, and the bases
easy.explanation: The passage mentions the pillars, the sea, the bases, and the residue of the vessels.
easy.q: Which objects are named in the list of vessels?

easy.explanation: The LORD says that they would be carried to Babylon.
easy.q: Where would the remaining vessels be carried?

answers: They would remain in Babylon forever
The LORD would bring them back to their place
easy.explanation: After the appointed time, the LORD would bring them up and restore them to their place.
easy.q: What would eventually happen to the vessels?

answers: Until the day that the LORD visited them
medium.explanation: They would remain there until the day that the LORD visited them.
medium.q: How long would the vessels remain in Babylon?

answers: The exile is temporary, and restoration will come later
medium.explanation: The vessels would first be taken to Babylon and later restored.
medium.q: What relationship between exile and restoration is shown here?

answers: The appointed time when the LORD would act concerning them
A day when the vessels would be sold
A day when new vessels would be made
medium.explanation: It refers to the LORD’s appointed time to intervene and restore the vessels.
medium.q: What does “the day that I visit them” mean in context?

answers: The prophecy includes vessels that had not yet been taken
All the vessels were already in Babylon
The vessels had nothing to do with the temple
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes that the vessels still remaining in Jerusalem would also be carried away.
challenge.q: What does the detailed list of objects show?

answers: They reject an immediate return and point to a later restoration
They confirm that the vessels would return at once
They cancel the subject of the vessels
challenge.explanation: The vessels would remain in Babylon until the LORD’s appointed time, not return shortly.
challenge.q: How do these verses answer the false prophets’ promise?

answers: He determines both the time of exile and the time of return
challenge.explanation: The LORD declares both the removal of the vessels and the time when He will restore them.
challenge.q: What does the future restoration reveal about the LORD’s control?
